title: Update docker/distribution to v3.1.2 for CVE-2026-85747
body:
CVE-2026-85747 affects docker/distribution in versions prior to v3.1.2. This commmit updates the version used by the image and common packages to this version to ensure this CVE is not detected by scanners.

Since this is a major version change in the package, import locations needed to be updated. The usage appears to be limited to error codes that are just being made available at a different path.

The common package still has an indirect dependency on the older version due to its dependency on the older version of the image package. Once this internal dependency is updated, the indirect dependency on the old distribution package will be removed.

<!--- Please read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/containers/container-libs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before proceeding --->

comments.body:
> Since this is a major version change in the package, import locations needed to be updated. The usage appears to be limited to error codes that are just being made available at a different path.

Yes if the vulnerable component is not reachable from us than it is not important for us to patch this or even mention the CVE as part of the commit log.

Updating the dependency to the new module does make sense regardless though so I think this is likely fine regardless

No; also https://github.com/podman-container-tools/skopeo/issues/3002 .

- This does not fix any vulnerability so we just don’t need to.
- This effectively breaks API because out-of-c/image callers (like c/common here) do check for the error types, and those checks would no longer match. E.g. this immediately breaks Podman.

Now, what to do…
- One alternative is to just keep things as is forever because we have no strong reason not to.
- Another is to formally bump to `image/v6`, ugh. I ~committed to try extremely hard to avoid that after quickly getting from v1 to v5.
- Or we could just silently change the types, because we, strictly speaking, never (to my knowledge) explicitly promised to use the `docker/distribution` types… fine, but then _we should not make the same mistake again_ and actually define c/image-specific error types for the conditions callers care about;
  - and historically we didn’t do that also because detecting _meaningful_ error conditions is hard (see `isManifestUnknownError` and we saw at least one other case which was fixed sever-side), so we punted and just exposed the raw registry errors. Would we try to actually define useful error types here?

Either way we are not going to do this in a rush, and certainly we can’t just merge this without coordinating across users.

Thank you both for the feedback. I can appreciate that the affected code is not called by the libraries, though in some cases corporate scanners and security policies are not the most reasonable. I imagine creating custom error types would probably require some design and input from various maintainers... would you prefer I close this PR then?

>   * and historically we didn’t do that also because detecting _meaningful_ error conditions is hard (see `isManifestUnknownError` and we saw at least one other case which was fixed sever-side), so we punted and just exposed the raw registry errors. Would we try to actually define useful error types here?

FWIW the Go error matching design is weird/powerful enough that we can do both — have error types that simultaneously conform to protocol-level errors (“registry reported manifest not found”) and best-effort semantic errors (“we think this means the manifest does not exist”), and callers could then make their own decisions whether they trust our heuristics or whether they want their own.
